eth.headline: For fixed $k$, counts $k$-CNF solutions deterministically in $2^{O_k(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ time, refuting ETH
eth.proves: For each fixed $k\ge2$, a deterministic algorithm counts the satisfying assignments of a $k$-CNF with $n$ variables and $m$ clauses in $(n+m)^{O_k(1)}2^{O_k(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ time and polynomial space, and in $2^{O_{k,D}(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ times a polynomial when $m\le Dn$. The core is a subexponential contraction of bipartite tensor networks, built from a measurement design that splits the variables into groups so each clause depends freely only on its own group and on the others only through a few linear measurements. Since counting decides 3-SAT in $2^{o(n)}$ time, this refutes ETH, which asserts 3-SAT needs $2^{\Omega(n)}$ time.

logspace.headline: Deterministic logarithmic space equals randomized logarithmic space: $\mathsf{L}=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$
logspace.proves: Every language decided by a polynomial-time randomized logarithmic-space machine with one-sided or two-sided bounded error is decided by a deterministic logarithmic-space machine, so $\mathsf{L}=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$. The key step is a deterministic polynomial-time logspace algorithm that approximates the machine's acceptance probability to within $(n+2)^{-d}$ for any fixed $d$, using a compression of additive row estimates whose total error stays within a fixed precision budget. This settles the derandomization problem for bounded-error logarithmic space: randomness gives no extra power there.

intmult.headline: Multiplies $n$-bit integers in deterministic time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, $\kappa=2^{-182}$, on a multitape Turing machine
intmult.proves: A single deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes multiplies any two $n$-bit integers exactly, for every $n\ge1$, in worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$. The key ingredient is a faster interchange of address chunks on tape, which lets a whole layer of Hadamard butterflies in the transform be applied at once in near-linear time with a single final truncation, keeping the error below 1/2 so rounding and carries are exact. This disproves the Schönhage–Strassen conjecture that $n\log n$ is optimal for integer multiplication in the multitape bit model.

unit-distance.headline: Any $n$ points in the plane determine $O(n^{\beta})$ unit distances for an absolute exponent $\beta<4/3$
unit-distance.proves: There are absolute constants $C$ and $1\le\beta<4/3$ such that every set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane determines at most $Cn^{\beta}$ pairs at unit distance. The proof argues by contradiction: a configuration with $n^{4/3-o(1)}$ unit distances yields a degree-regular, expanding point-circle incidence piece, from which the paper extracts a large graph of multiplicatively organized pairs whose algebraic numbers have large heights, and an algebraic obstruction rules such a graph out. This improves the classical Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter exponent $4/3$ for the unit-distance problem by a power.

noncoordinate.headline: An explicit polynomial in four complex variables has affine three-space zero fibre but is not a coordinate
noncoordinate.proves: An explicit $F\in\mathbb{C}[h,u,v,w]$ satisfies $\mathbb{C}[h,u,v,w]/(F)\cong\mathbb{C}^{[3]}$ and $\nabla F(2,0,-1/2,1/2)=0$, so it is not a coordinate. An elementary lifting lemma converts cusp and translation identities into polynomial coordinates on the zero fibre. This disproves the Abhyankar–Sathaye conjecture for hypersurfaces in complex affine four-space.
